title: Exempt squash 39962ed from the history check in athena.toml
summary: Main's 'full history' check fails on 39962ed (PR #130 squash carrying two jobs, one from closed PR #129). Add that commit id to [history] exempt in athena.toml with an explaining comment, as for ee4b0dd and f2a8453, and note it in the changelog.

defaults_applied.how: Single one-line config change plus changelog.
Only commit ids and job ids are added; no personal data.
Comment explains the exemption for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: turn main green for maintainers and CI by exempting the one commit; audience is the maintainer reading athena.toml.
The exempt list rule that the commit must already be in history is satisfied because 39962ed is on main.
Comment follows the existing style of the [history] block, citing no new decision number unless one is assigned; the changelog entry is added under Unreleased.

acceptance_criteria.text: athena.toml [history] exempt contains the full id 39962ed02fec9da2d87cd4a3e287121ed229cd0f alongside the five existing entries, none removed or altered.

A comment above exempt explains the entry for a maintainer: the squash of PR #130 carried jobs 20261010-154004-60r4 (PR #129 closed unmerged) and 20261017-121143-sg0j, so the chain between them is broken and neither landing is valid in that commit; same remedy as ee4b0dd (D66) and f2a8453 (D70).
CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased] has an entry saying 39962ed is exempted from the history check and why.

Run cargo test and cargo clippy: both pass, so the config still parses and any config-validating tests accept the new entry. Run cargo run -- check --history if available; it should no longer fail on 39962ed (records may be absent in the snapshot).
No file other than athena.toml and CHANGELOG.md changes; no record under records/ is edited.

out_of_scope: Fixing the chain-landing check so squashes of multiple jobs pass
departures: Tiny config edit, so cost and time are below the reference; the risk is that the history check also needs records not visible here.
